findings.where: Screens 1 and 7 (SHOW text plus the caption under the picture)
findings.what: With the live caption that sits after the diagrams, screen 1 runs to about 114 words (88 + 26) and screen 7 to about 104 (83 + 21), over the 90-word limit, with screens 3 (about 99) and 9 (about 97) on the line; cut the main text or drop the caption sentences that repeat it.

"Fundamental" is the yardstick for every number on the harmonics card ("1/h as tall as the fundamental", the THD ratio) but no sentence says it is the sine at the supply frequency; add that one sentence and highlight it with harmonics.

"Remember triplens adding in a neutral?" asks him to recall a word he never met, because AC circuits lesson 10 only said that harmonics at three times the supply frequency add in the neutral; say that instead, or define triplen here.

The practice text has 12 footnote markers, nearly one per line (17, 8, 7, 14, 10, 11, 20, 2, 21, 22, 18, 23), against the rule of a few per lesson; keep them only on what he would look up on a job (the 5 and 15 minute waits, Type B, the 3.5 mA touch current) and remove the rest. The explanation carries 10 more wherever it is shown.

The question is about a 60 Hz supply, but the spectrum opens at 50 Hz with "250" printed under the 5th bar, which is the distractor, and the frequency switch is hidden, so the only Hz the picture shows for the 5th is the wrong one; open it with the Hz row hidden or at 60 Hz with the 5th's label hidden until Check.

findings.where: Screen 3 text and screen 4's hint for the 10th
findings.what: The reason no even harmonic appears is thin, and the hint "An even harmonic needs halves that differ. These mirror." is confusing because mirror-image halves do differ; say that an even harmonic is the same in both half cycles while the block flips sign, so the block cannot contain one, and say that n is any whole number in 6n ± 1.

The text jumps from "the L2 and L3 capacitors see 400 V" to "21.8 mA" without saying each passes 12.6 mA and that the two are 60° apart. That 21.8 mA is about three times one capacitor's 7.2 mA, so it looks like screen 10's wrong answer "21.6 mA, all three added". Say the fault draws three capacitors' worth, and round both from the same line-to-earth voltage so the two figures do not differ by 0.2.
"returns through earth, past the RCD" can read as going around the RCD unseen, when the point is that the RCD sees it as leakage; say "so the RCD sees it" in the text, as the caption already does.

findings.where: Put it into practice, worked example
findings.what: Checked by hand: 254 V, 26.5 kΩ, 9.6 mA and 28.7 mA are all correct. But "nearly all of a 30 mA RCD's rating" undersells the result, because a 30 mA RCD may trip anywhere above half its rating, which Dan knows from testing them; say that it would very likely trip, and that two such drives could.

The picture and its 7.2 mA readout show the AC leakage with a phase lost, not the DC-link fault the question asks about, and no screen shows why a drive's earth fault can carry smooth DC; the question has to hand him the key fact. Draw a DC-link fault case, or hide the unrelated readout.
"the filter's capacitors charge through it" skips the step that the monitor reads any current between the system and earth as lost insulation; add one sentence on how it sees the charging current.

findings.where: Screen 11, caption for "Insulated, fault, filter out"
findings.what: "the fault has no return path and draws 0 mA" states the model's simplification as fact. A real insulated system's cable capacitance lets a first fault draw a small current, and Dan works on insulated systems. Say "almost nothing", as the screen's own text does.

"Twelve-pulse rectifiers" and "Eighteen-pulse ones" arrive with no word on what they are; one short sentence (more bridges fed out of step, so the 5th and 7th cancel) would make the comparison bars mean something.

Each demonstration plays as the screen opens and finishes in 2.4 to 4.5 s. At 360 px the picture sits below about 470 px of text, so on a phone it plays out of sight while he reads, and there is no replay because the motion button is off. Start it when the picture comes into view, or offer a replay.
"THE 5TH AT 60 / HZ" breaks the number from its unit across lines in light and dark; join them with a non-breaking space.

findings.where: Sines added slider, screens 1 and 5 at 360 px
findings.what: The end labels "Fundamental only" and "Every harmonic" nearly run together under the track and read as one phrase; shorten them ("Fundamental", "Every one") or put them on separate lines.

findings.where: Leakage card, screens 9, 10 and 13 at 360 px
findings.what: The red "fuse blown" label touches the blown-fuse symbol. The phasor figure is small, with wide empty space beside it, and the dashed end-to-end arrowhead overlaps the sum's arrowhead; enlarge the phasors and move the label clear.

The brief says the last screens are a mixed set from the whole course, but both final puzzles test only this lesson. The promised recall question on AC lesson 10's neutral current is folded into screen 3's text rather than asked.

findings.where: Lesson as a whole (brief section 2, lesson 8)
findings.what: The brief's EMC line is missing: the line filter's working band, the shielded motor cable bonded 360 degrees and the C1 to C4 categories. Either give the cable screen one sentence on screen 9, or note the gap.
